Trusted server-side authorization inputs; these are not request DTOs.

The authenticated principal and selected assignment must be loaded by a service.

``authoritative_not_found`` means lookup returning not_found guarantees that
retrying the original dedupe identity is safe, including an earlier request
that is still in flight. Eventual-consistency absence is insufficient.

app/delivery/worker.py.doc:
Short-transaction outbox ownership, external I/O, and fenced receipts.

This worker is deliberately not wired into an application or HTTP endpoint.
The composition root must supply a real current-authorization adapter and
reviewed sinks. The clock/leases assume the current single-host deployment;
cross-host clock and fencing protocols require separate verification.

classes.name: OutboxWorker
classes.doc:
Own delivery tasks until close completes, with no implicit authorization.

``run_once`` only sends pending messages. Unknown messages require explicit
``reconcile_one``; it never sends. Reconciliation appends a separate attempt
and preserves the original uncertain attempt. An authoritative absence is
recorded as a failed reconciliation attempt with ``reconcile.not_found``;
only a sink promising both deduplication and safe absence can requeue it.

Start standalone polling and return its observable task.

Poll until stopped; a fault stops intake and propagates to the owner.

No implicit restart is safe: a failed claim/receipt commit may have an
unknown outcome. Recovery uses persisted leases and reconciliation.

functions.doc: Observe polling completion/failure without cancelling its owner task.

functions.name: OutboxWorker.close
functions.doc:
Stop intake and await owned I/O and durable cancellation bookkeeping.

A noncooperative sink cannot be forcibly terminated inside Python. If
tasks remain live this raises, retaining their ownership; the host must
not dispose shared dependencies or claim a completed drain.

functions.name: _finish_cleanup
functions.doc:
Finish session cleanup even when the owner task was cancelled.

SQLAlchemy asyncpg rollback/close can outlive the cancellation that stopped
a worker. Running each operation in its own task and waiting through a
shield prevents the pool from being disposed while the transaction still
owns a connection.

Lock an explicitly provisioned tenant; never create one from caller input.

SQLite needs a write reservation because SELECT FOR UPDATE is ignored.
PostgreSQL uses row locking. All relevant trusted writers must use this
same guard; this helper cannot protect against arbitrary out-of-band SQL.

classes.name: UTCDateTime
classes.doc:
Use timestamptz on PostgreSQL and explicit UTC wall time elsewhere.

Naive values are rejected on write. Naive reads are only interpreted as UTC
for MySQL/SQLite, where this adapter deliberately stores UTC without a zone.
The migration requires an explicit acknowledgement before adopting old data.

classes.name: ExactString
classes.doc:
Identifiers and machine values use case/accent/space sensitive comparison.

Display names should remain ordinary String/Text columns. PostgreSQL uses
C collation and SQLite uses BINARY. The historical MySQL mapping is retained
for migration/DDL checks; MySQL is no longer an application database target.
